sections.html:
Loveland is a home rule city in southeastern Larimer County, about 46 miles north of the State Capitol in Denver. The 2020 census counted 76,378 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 81,387. Thompson R2-J runs the public schools.

Growth came in waves. The population stood at 16,220 in 1970, reached 30,215 by 1980 and hit 76,378 by 2020, so the city holds houses from several building booms. Many residents commute to Fort Collins, Greeley, Boulder or the Denver area, and tourists pass through on the way to Estes Park, so buyers come from several directions.

sections.h2: Flood questions near the Big Thompson
sections.html:
Two historic floods hit the Big Thompson watershed, and both color how people talk about property here. The 1976 Big Thompson Flood killed 144 people. The flood of September 12, 2013 followed four days of heavy rain, collapsed sections of U.S. Highway 34 and killed two people in Larimer County. Loveland itself saw about 4 inches of rain, far less than the mountains upstream.

If you own near the river, ask the city or county whether your parcel sits in a mapped floodplain. A buyer, lender or insurer will ask the same thing, and knowing the answer early keeps a sale from stalling.

Average snowfall is 47 inches a year, and summers run warm to hot. Snow load, freeze and thaw cycles and summer heat all wear on roofs, gutters and exterior paint. If your house has a deferred roof or a tired furnace, price those items before you list.

Lake Loveland, an early irrigation reservoir inside city limits, adds one local wrinkle. Public fishing is available from public shorelines, but recreation rights on the lake belong to the homeowners whose lots surround it. If your lot borders the lake, tell buyers what that means for them.

sections.h2: Larimer County valuation and tax dates
sections.html:

First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Colorado treasurers follow this pattern, and taxes are collected one year in arrears. Call the Larimer County Treasurer for the exact dates this year, and ask your closing agent how the current year's tax will be handled at the table.

Larimer County reappraises all real property every two years, in odd-numbered years, and owners get a Notice of Valuation in May. The Assessor's Office at (970) 498-7050 can discuss a value with you. If you plan to sell in a reappraisal year, read the notice, since the figure shapes the buyer's tax bill.
Colorado charges a documentary fee of 1 cent per $100 on transfers above $500, set by state law. Every recorded deed also needs the buyer's mailing address. Who pays the fee is a contract term.

Loveland runs under a home rule, council-manager form of government. Permits, code questions and utility accounts for a Loveland address go through the city. Start there when you need to confirm what a buyer will ask about the property, such as open permits or a final utility reading.

sections.h2: Choosing how to sell a Loveland house
sections.html:
A Loveland house can be listed, sold by the owner or sold for cash, and each route trades time against effort. A listing brings the widest buyer pool but also repairs, showings and inspection negotiations. A cash sale is faster and usually as-is.

If the house is inherited, rented out or behind on payments, say so up front. Those details change the paperwork more than the price conversation, and our team can walk through them with you before you decide anything.

You describe the property, and we review it. If an offer works for you, a title company confirms ownership, checks the Larimer County tax status, prepares the deed and handles recording. At the signing, taxes and any loan balance are paid out of the proceeds, and you receive the rest. With no lender, no appraisal holds up the date, so you can choose a closing that matches your move.

Collect your latest valuation notice and tax bill, any mortgage payoff statement, and records of roof, furnace or window work. If you own near the river or the lake, add anything you have on floodplain status or lake rights. For an inherited house, bring proof of who may sign. For a rental, bring the lease and the rent history. Organized records let the title company work in parallel instead of waiting on you.

An inherited house raises the same questions in every town: who can sign, what is owed, and who will handle the upkeep meanwhile. Settle the first before you ask for offers. Then find out the tax status with the Larimer County Treasurer and whether any mortgage remains. Keep the lawn mowed, the heat set and the utilities on until closing, because a neglected house loses value quickly and may raise questions with insurers. If heirs live out of state, a single closing with electronic signing avoids repeated trips.

sections.h2: Selling a rental that tenants occupy
sections.html: Owners who have had enough of managing a rental can sell without waiting for a lease to end. Share the lease and the rent roll, say whether the tenants plan to stay, and the buyer will price the arrangement. A buyer who keeps the tenants takes over the lease terms, so describe them accurately. If you would rather hand over a vacant house, give the buyer a realistic move-out date so the closing can be timed to match. Either way, the title company confirms the lease details with the buyer before the deed is signed, and deposits are settled on the closing statement. Gather any security deposit records early, since the buyer will want to know what is held and where. A prompt answer keeps the closing statement accurate and avoids a last-day scramble over deposit amounts at the signing table.

Owners who are behind on the mortgage or on taxes sometimes assume nothing can be done. A sale can still work. The title company pays off balances from the proceeds at closing, so what matters is that the sale price covers what is owed and that you act before the situation worsens. Ask the lender for a payoff figure and the treasurer for the tax balance, and bring both to the first conversation.

List with an agent and you take on cleaning, photographs, showings, offers, the buyer's inspection and an appraisal, then a wait while the buyer's lender finishes underwriting. If the appraisal comes in low or the loan stalls, you may be back at the start. Selling for cash skips those steps. The trade-off is the price, since a buyer who absorbs repairs and speed will offer less than a polished listing might reach. Decide what your time and peace of mind are worth.

faqs.q: What county is Loveland, CO in?
faqs.a: Southeastern Larimer County. The county seat is Fort Collins, and the Larimer County Assessor handles valuation for Loveland homes.

faqs.q: How often does Larimer County reappraise homes?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years. Owners receive a Notice of Valuation in May.
Loveland is near the Big Thompson River, which flooded severely in 1976 and again in 2013. Ask the city or county whether your parcel is in a mapped floodplain.
The Thompson R2-J School District runs Loveland's public schools.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Loveland house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is and prices the roof into the offer, so you do not have to replace it first.
